about: Which checks cover which files. node checks/run.mjs --changed reads this; a file no rule matches runs everything. Smoke entries are pieces of a section title in checks/smoke-shell.mjs (node checks/smoke-parallel.mjs --list shows them); "*" is every section, or every Node check.

store.covers: undo, autosave, folder mirror, backup, checkpoints

paginate.covers: block pagination, Fit on the last page, labels, photo, fields

direct.covers: the model behind editing on the page: cut-off, parked edits, lines only on one resume, every printed text as an edit with its base, headings, a language's name, the lock on every function that changes locked content, hiding a block that holds a lock, a reset layout, stale locks, a restore, the record's own edits, the Review list's model (a sub-version copies the source, a new major or claim needs one, Update changes the nearest version and the other resumes see newer wording, headings and names, a line only here becomes a claim, one undo step)

review-model.covers: the Review list's model (and a line's earlier edits: stacked, shown, thrown away, made a version by themselves): no draft or archived version as a parent or pick, a duplicate keeps its held lines, an equal heading is not listed, highlights follow trimmed text, the other resumes an update or a heading change reaches

multilingual.covers: language copies kept in step both ways (order, hiding, picks, sections, locks, the look), what each keeps its own, picks matched by number, behind and missing at a number, new numbers over every language, addVersion's n, one undo, old copies and other resumes untouched, headings and other labels written against the other language's words (labelFrom, i18n from), one-off texts listed elsewhere, matchNumber and guessMatch

diff.covers: the merge engine on an edited copy of the example

merge.covers: merging an older copy: what you deleted (a claim, a version, a saved resume, a sent copy) is listed, not added; a version of another text in a copy of the same career is an unticked change; the same file twice adds nothing; five copies merged in any order end byte-identical; a merged version keeps its source; normText; every saved resume prints the same. Object clocks (version vectors): keys and ticks, a save counted once, two devices that edited different things end byte-identical with one clock, a version both reworded or both added, the later edit wins a plain value, a delete against an edit (the one that has seen the other is later, else the edit wins), tombstones travel, a device whose clock runs behind, many saves between two files, a file edited outside, a garbled clock, deletes keeping every claim valid, version numbers unique across three copies, an Undo that sticks, tags of two copies joined, two new objects under one id kept as two (a certificate, a version), reword/delete/reword in any order, a file met twice, deletion marks in one order, language groups as one unit, and a random run of 2 to 5 copies with saved resumes and a language group (FUZZ_SEEDS=n, FUZZ_FIRST=n, FUZZ_ALL=1 to count every failing seed)

documents.covers: documents in the state (src/model/documents.js): the id from the file's sha256, the same file twice or on two devices is one document, a backup round-trips documents, rounds and the import log (an older file with none opens with no warnings, and so does code that ignores them), a clocked merge keeps both sides' documents, rounds and log, another format of one resume (sameDocument), inFile finds an original in a saved backup, an embedded original stays out of the undo steps and checkpoints (stored once, older inline checkpoints still restore) and keepTextOnly frees it, the 10 MB limit, safety's every outcome, a round or archived flag changes no printed page, one file on two devices joins without a line (but keep text only against an edit is listed), a delete against an edit of a document, the list in one order with three copies, saving reads no original back and a failing clean-up fails nothing, folder checkpoints and library.json carry documents text-only, the one-file tool says which originals it cannot carry

parse.covers: the resume parser (src/parse/, a port of OpenResume's): text items in, JSON Resume out with a trace and leftovers, for one column and two (split only when sure: a header band over a sidebar, a right sidebar; one column with a doubt when a column is seen but not trusted: indented lists, places on right-aligned lines, rows that never meet; a layout given by hand wins) with the layout used and the doubts returned, and Hungarian and German headings and dates given a lexicon built from the catalogue, the lexicon from the English catalogue changes nothing, a line that fits nowhere is left over, every ported file names its OpenResume source and commit, and nothing in src/parse/ imports from outside it. The readers: identify by the bytes whatever the name (PDF, Word, Google Docs, ODT, Pages, LinkedIn, HTML, Markdown, text, JSON, images, other), unzip (stored and deflated entries, ZIP64, encrypted, damaged and over-large refused), DOCX as Word and as Google Docs write it (headings by style name, lists, tabs, bold from runs and styles, text boxes once), ODT, HTML, Markdown and text giving the one-column resume's JSON Resume with whole lines, no column and no doubt, the same lines in every format (sameDocument links them), only extraction damage mended in the text of every item (quotes and dashes stay), headings titles only at the document's top level, a LinkedIn export with renamed headers in the parser's shape, real-world inputs (HTML fragments, XHTML, SVG, an .ods, a cut or ZIP64 file giving unzip's error, images, an open <li>, entities, comments, hidden parts; Word text boxes, hidden text, deleted paragraphs, headers and footers; ODT links, notes, frames and deletions; setext headings, front matter, reference links; only the header and footer the last section uses, not read but coming back as leftovers (section header or footer) with page numbers in ten languages and repeats dropped; two spaces as a gap except after a full stop; tracked-change properties and moved-away text; open elements ending at their parent; CDATA, pre, the code empty; Central European entities), one 64 MB budget for all the reads of a ZIP, 30,000 repeats of a broken tag finishing in under a second, parseCsv in src/parse/csv.js, and documents formatted by hand (no heading styles: headings larger, coloured, underlined or in Word's caps, typed and symbol-font bullets, Shift+Enter lines, a sidebar table read column by column, spaced-letter headings, the name larger, dates by tab; in Word, ODT and HTML with inline styles, each giving the one-column resume's JSON Resume; the look of every run through Word's style chain, ODT styles and inline CSS; when a short line is a title by its look and when not; the doubt for a file with no jobs; company and job-title lines with a title word inside, links, taglines and the contact block that must not become sections; symbol-font bullets against other symbols; layout tables with a merged header; hostile lines that must read in seconds; the letter doubt (an English and a German cover letter, not a resume with a long summary, not a file with a date range or a section title) and no jobs doubt for a letter; paragraphs under a work heading with no job line left over whole, one each, and kept in a dated job's highlights; an old .doc and a modern Pages file named by identify and readPages)

direct-c-check.covers: UX-6 direct editing round 2, builder C: the plate's tint in hover and selected in the four looks, the look ladder (hover wash per drink, selected x1.5 with a 1px edge, writing, one corner, the timings), the hover zones (a slow path through the gaps shows a big plate only on a heading row), the grip in the plate (dots on approach, a tab where the words leave room, a clear button inside the plate, touch), the plate across a camera ease as writing starts, the drag lighter (1 px edge, wash, small lift) and tighter (12 px give across a one-axis list, 12 px bumper), the hands riding the page frame by frame through a pan and a zoom, the snap drag (lag cap, the pop at halfway) and the free drag behind ?drag=free

plate-check.covers: the plate, the one selection system (UX-6f 4b): the selection classes the page's frame knows are exactly the plate's and every rule of one takes its outline, shadow, radius and fill from the --plate-* tokens, the tokens reach the frame in Tea and Coffee, light and dark, each class on a line, a group, a job and a section draws what the tokens say, hover, selected (with the ring trail), writing and lifted (with its dashed socket) per level, the preview accent in the plate's shape, the grip as the plate's tab; hover is intent: a fast sweep across blocks or off the page draws no plate, a slow one shows the block it stops on and one at a time (and cross-fades), a stop after a fast sweep shows it within 150 ms, a press, a grip in focus and an arrow step show theirs at once, leaving the page cancels it, into the sidebar and out leaves nothing, under reduced motion too

overlap-check.covers: nothing the app draws over the page overlaps another of its marks or printed text it is not about (UX-6f 4c): the plate and its ring trail, the grip, the "+", the version tools, the depth chip, the socket, the drop line, the rail, the card, the search, preview and missing-text marks, the zoom bar and the photo slot, on a line (first, middle, last of a job), a skill group, a job, a section and a header line, at rest, hovered, mid-glide, selected, written and lifted, in Tea and Coffee, light and dark, at fit and 130%, with motion and reduced, in a narrow window and at phone width, in English and German; the allowed pairs are named in checks/lib/overlap.mjs

room-check.covers: the sidebar and the layout around the page: hidden share of the body, nothing too wide, the page filling the height
